scope: CURSORS MEASURED: the byte cursor sits at byte 164 of a 172-byte body when the entity block reads the count, while the bit cursor is much further on - the two really are independent

measurement.breakpoint: 0x671650:Cursor (function entry, a shape that has worked before)

what_these_fields_are.+0x14: 172 = the total LENGTH of our snapshot body (snapshot-single22.bin is 172 bytes) - confirmed by the file size
what_these_fields_are.+0x1C: 164 = the BYTE CURSOR position when the entity block starts
what_these_fields_are.+0x24: 0xFFFFFFFF = the sentinel the caller writes before each block (seen at 0x4723CF and 0x4723F3)

the_actionable_conclusion: the entity COUNT is read from byte offset 164 of the body
the formula in 0x66ED70 is: bound = [+0x18] + [+0x14] = 172, cursor = [+0x1C] = 164, so the byte read is body[164]
the bit cursor is around bit 1350 at that moment, i.e. a completely different position - so the two cursors are indeed independent, and the count is NOT where a pure bit model would put it
therefore: to make the entity count equal 1, body byte 164 must be 0x01
why_this_is_the_most_actionable_finding_: it is a single byte in a file we control
no bit-level construction is needed to test it - patch body[164] = 0x01 and read 0x7859558
and if the count becomes 1, the block will then read 12 bits per entity id from the BIT stream, which the encoder already handles
next: patch byte 164 of runs/snapshot-single22.bin to 0x01, run, and read 0x7859558
if it reads 1, the entity list is finally non-empty and the next question is the per-entity payload
